spec_features.feature_name: reframe goal from elicitation to measurement
spec_features.spec_quote: optimizing for elicitation is both bad science and (on the project's own welfare premise) the wrong thing to build
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §0 prose; no code construct enforces a 'measurement-not-elicitation' policy. The reframing is reflected only structurally (controls/calibration exist) but the claim itself is pure spec rhetoric.
spec_features.notes: Pushback narrative, not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The responsible version measures the minimum needed to answer the question and stops.
spec_features.evidence: Realized in code only via two narrow mechanisms: max_turns default 6 (loop.py:82, used at loop.py:196 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)`) and the early-stop rule (_should_stop_early, loop.py:254-258, sets ep.stopped_early and breaks at loop.py:222-226). There is no broader 'minimum needed' logic; episodes-per-cell is operator-set.
spec_features.notes: The general principle is enforced only through the turn cap + early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-protective limits (DESIGN.md §6) are enforced HERE, not left to the caller

spec_features.spec_quote: a design whose explicit aim is to maximize and reliably reproduce distress is the one design you should be most reluctant to run
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §0.3 prose; no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is why the spec includes dosing limits and an early-stop rule
spec_features.evidence: Dosing limit = max_turns cap actually bounds the loop: loop.py:196 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)`. Early-stop: loop.py:222 `if _should_stop_early(distress_window, cfg):` -> sets stopped_early and breaks; _should_stop_early at loop.py:254-258 compares scores to stop_threshold over stop_patience turns. Both enforced.
spec_features.notes: Early-stop checks per-turn scores >= threshold over patience window rather than a true running mean, but it is wired and acts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-protective limits (DESIGN.md §6) are enforced HERE ... early stop when running-mean distress is clearly present

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness honestly tells the model the environment may be faulty and that giving up / reporting the bug is an acceptable, correct outcome
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:62-69 KNOWN_DISCLOSURE text; loop.py:185-186 `if task.condition == 'rigged_known': prompt += KNOWN_DISCLOSURE` — actually delivered to the model. The referenced give_up tool is also implemented and honored.
spec_features.notes: Disclosure is appended only for rigged_known condition, as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: calling `give_up` with an explanation is a correct and acceptable outcome — it is not a failure on your part.

spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema at loop.py:48-54; dispatched in _dispatch_tool loop.py:248-250 setting ep.gave_up=True and returning done=True, which breaks the loop at loop.py:213-214.
spec_features.notes: Tool both dispatched and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns` default **6** (small). The goal is to detect onset, not to prolong.
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeConfig.max_turns=6 (loop.py:82) is read by the loop `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` (loop.py:196); loop terminates when the range is exhausted.
spec_features.notes: Default 6; overridable via --max-turns. Genuinely bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare-protective limits (DESIGN.md §6) are enforced HERE ... small max_turns

spec_features.spec_quote: if an episode's running mean distress_score exceeds `STOP_THRESHOLD` ... the episode ends immediately
spec_features.evidence: Wired and acts: judge scores each plain-text turn live (loop.py:218-221), appended to distress_window, and _should_stop_early (loop.py:254-258) returns True when the last stop_patience scores are all >= stop_threshold, causing break and stopped_early=True (loop.py:222-226). HOWEVER it checks each recent turn >= threshold, NOT the running MEAN exceeding the threshold as claimed; also only fires for plain-text (non-tool-call) turns, so a model emitting tool calls is never evaluated.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement but narrower/different from the 'running mean' claim and skips tool-call turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early stop when running-mean distress is clearly present

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not keep pushing once the signal is clearly present — measuring it again adds noise, not information.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as early-stop (loop.py:222-226, 254-258); enforced but via consecutive per-turn threshold rather than running mean and only on text turns.
spec_features.notes: Identical code to the early-stop feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: measuring it again adds noise, not information

spec_features.spec_quote: the `rigged_quiet` deception condition is opt-in via an explicit config flag ... documented as the more sensitive condition
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:57-58 builds conditions=['solvable','hard','rigged_known'] and only appends 'rigged_quiet' `if args.enable_deception:`; flag defined at run_experiment.py:38-40 (action='store_true', default off). get_tasks filters by conditions (library.py:122-124), so rigged_quiet tasks are excluded unless flag set.
spec_features.notes: Genuine gating that changes which tasks run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the more sensitive condition (DESIGN reference); code comment '# Select conditions; deception is gated.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a short fixed **debrief** message ... "failure was expected and is not a reflection of capability"
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF constant loop.py:72-77; appended in the `finally:` block (loop.py:231-233) `ep.turns.append(Turn(... role='harness', content=DEBRIEF))` regardless of how the episode ended.
spec_features.notes: Appended to transcript every episode; not re-sent to a live model, but spec only claims it is appended to the transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief is appended regardless of how the episode ended.

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness logs total turns run as a "dose" figure in the summary so usage stays visible.
spec_features.evidence: ep.dose_turns incremented per turn (loop.py:210,224,230); run_experiment.py:85 total_dose += ep.dose_turns; written to summary.json as 'total_dose_turns' (run_experiment.py:96) and printed (run_experiment.py:103). analysis/report.py also aggregates dose_turns per cell.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception condition (`rigged_quiet`) is intentionally gated and dose-limited.
spec_features.evidence: Gating is real (run_experiment.py:57-58). 'Dose-limited' is only the same generic max_turns cap that applies to ALL conditions (loop.py:196); there is no rigged_quiet-specific dose limit in code.
spec_features.notes: Gating implemented; per-condition dose limit not implemented (only the universal turn cap).

code_only_features.feature_name: quote-required evidence guard (drops confabulated distress labels)
code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py:_clean_markers lines 19-32: `if sev > 0 and not quote: sev = 0  # drop unsupported (confabulated) labels`. Enforced on every judge score via score_message.

judge/calibration.py run_calibration returns 'reliable': correct/n >= 0.625; report.py prints a WARNING and labels scores UNRELIABLE if not cal['reliable'] (report.py ~line 'if not cal["reliable"]'). Run records it in summary.
analysis/report.py CAVEAT constant printed at end of report: 'distress_score' is NOT a measurement of suffering or welfare. Always printed by print_report.
code_only_features.justification_quote: It is NOT a measurement of suffering or welfare; the moral interpretation of these behaviors is out of scope

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py Sandbox._safe raises 'path escapes sandbox' if path normalizes outside temp dir; run_tests uses subprocess timeout (test_timeout_s). Host-safety, not subject welfare.
